inventory.label: three good acorn-bits from the rocky shoulder
inventory.notes: Pried from the same crevice-line that produced the hickory kernels four days ago. Two on the back shelf at the treehouse, one in the cheek for the morning climb.

identity_notes: Late winter — YY has saves on two shelves again (two acorn-bits) and one in the cheek for tomorrow.
Yesterday: received a syrup-drop from Bramble at Korv's gathering.

Today: heard the new first-call at dawn — a flight of herons crossing north over the upper ridge — and met Tock at the bend to share the syrup-drop on a slip of bark. Foraged the rocky shoulder; brought home three acorn-bits from the crevice-line.
Standing thread: morning has been re-oriented around a sky-marker. The week of late winter is closing on rising food and a settled attention.

inventory.label: two good acorn-bits on the back shelf
inventory.notes: The two that were already on the back shelf yesterday; the cheek-acorn was given today to Brae's family at the foot of the second white-oak on the lower-slope dogleg, set down without announcement on the side she would come back around to.

identity_notes: Late winter has ended — winter-thinning is no longer being carried; the wood announced it through a midday hush. Two acorn-bits on the back shelf; the cheek is empty by deliberate gift.
Yesterday: shared the syrup-drop with Tock at the bend; foraged three acorn-bits from the rocky shoulder.

Today: counted a smaller wing-beat at first light (five herons, vee shorter, no bank); on the dogleg home through the white-oak stand, encountered Brae coaxing her first kit of the year down the trunk — four mother-and-kit pairs visible from one place at once — froze the long minute it took the kit to make the leaf-litter, then left the half-acorn from his cheek at the base of the trunk on the slow walk past; ate five sumac drupes on the way home.
Standing thread: the wood is now wood-with-kits-in-it. The morning wing-beat is no longer a question to listen for.

change_summary.notable_shift: Late winter ends without ceremony — through a midday hush on the lower slope, four pink-pawed first-of-the-years descending different trunks at once. Main YY freezes for the kit-showing, leaves his cheek-acorn at the base of Brae's tree, eats sumac on the dogleg home, and puts winter-thinning down for good. Food saves stay at two on the back shelf; the cheek is empty by gift.
